messages.content: What is the status and scheduled trial date for case number XY1234 in Los Angeles County Court, and case number GH5678 in Orange County Court?

function.name: court_info_get_case_status
function.description: Retrieves the status and trial dates for court cases from specified county courts. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

court.description: The county court where the case is filed.

details.description: Specific details required about the court case. Defaults to 'status'.

We need to call the function twice or once with multiple? The function signature expects case_number, court, details optional. We can call it twice: first for XY1234 in Los Angeles County Court, second for GH5678 in Orange County Court. Provide details: status and trial_date. But the function only accepts one detail at a time? It says details?: "status" | "trial_date". So we might need two calls per case. But maybe we can pass details default 'status' and then get status; then call again for trial_date. Or we could call once for each case with details unspecified (default status). Then call again for trial_date. That would be 4 calls. But maybe we can combine? The function doesn't support multiple details. So we need 4 calls.

But maybe we can ask the function to return both? The description says "Specific details required about the court case. Defaults to 'status'." So we can't request both at once. So we need separate calls.

Thus we will call function for XY1234 Los Angeles County Court status, then XY1234 Los Angeles County Court trial_date, then GH5678 Orange County Court status, then GH5678 Orange County Court trial_date.

We should output the results after calling. We'll use the function calls.
